sourceVersions.provenance: Info.plist CFBundleIdentifier com.openai.codex; readArchive/readEntry extraction only
Contract pinned optional SQACPHost source; availability gated by Memex Package.swift build configuration

coverage.examinedBoundaries: Codex settings applicability map -> settings implementations/app-server calls and desktop tool schemas. Memex native Settings/menus/sidebar/library, composer catalogs/runtime connection, host request allowlist/schedule runtime, notification state machine. Read-only; no runtime claims.
coverage.disposition: Seven findings; performance and accessibility quality unknown; sidebar snooze intentionally excluded; Work/Pages/cloud-only capabilities excluded from coding parity.

findings.capability: Install, configure, authenticate and remove plugins/custom MCP servers
findings.userWorkflow: Install, configure, authenticate and remove plugins/custom MCP servers
findings.comparatorState: Codex-local/work-local settings route exposes plugin management subject to capability gates; custom MCP editor supports stdio and streamable HTTP, saves/uninstalls, and dispatches OAuth login. Plugin installation dispatch reaches app-server plugin/install.
findings.memexState: Memex discovers local skill/command files and uses native provider runtimes, but has no plugin/MCP management UI. Optional runtime plugin startup support is not passed by Memex resume connection. This does not mean native provider-configured tools cannot run.
findings.validationLevel: inspected source; no runtime action or UI verification

evidence.claim: Routes bind MCP management to Codex or local Work; skills-settings standalone route explicitly hidden.
Custom MCP form Ui validates transport fields and delegates onSave/onUninstall; includes STDIO/streamable_http fields.
Per-host authenticate action executes MCP OAuth login, validates URL then opens external browser.
Installation helper pun sends plugin/install to host app-server.
Catalog implements local skills/commands discovery, not installation/authentication.
Memex existing Codex connection passes executable/environment only.
Runtime capability exists but defaults to nil; no native Memex management caller.
Native Settings scene is empty; native menus route execution hosts/schedules and workspace controls. App source inventory has no plugin manager.

findings.implication: Users must manage tools through provider configuration or other apps even though local skills can be selected in Memex.
findings.recommendation: Prioritize a bounded per-provider MCP inventory/configuration/OAuth surface; do not invent one universal provider plugin contract.
caveats: Codex plugin marketplace access depends on host/account capabilities. Installed UI confirmation belongs to root.
Absence is native Memex management UI, not absence of MCP execution in its providers.

findings.capability: Create recurring work and inspect its runs
findings.userWorkflow: Create recurring work and inspect its runs
findings.comparatorState: Codex automation source supports heartbeat linked to a thread, cron project targets, run-now/pause, run history and per-automation notification policy.
findings.memexState: Memex already supports durable host schedules on existing conversations, interval or timezone+weekday wall-clock recurrence, edit/pause/run/delete and held-queue recovery. It lacks the standalone new-chat-per-run target and dedicated run inbox/per-schedule notification policy in inspected host model/UI.
findings.validationLevel: inspected source; no runtime action or UI verification

evidence.claim: Automation page handles thread-linked heartbeats distinctly; later create/run-now dispatches and history actions are wired.
Draft editor exposes per-automation notification policy including failed_runs_only; kind heartbeat and model/reasoning are separate draft fields.
Cron-specific target/project and template state separated from heartbeat.
Reachable host sheet supports schedules and explicit recurrence, run, edit, pause and delete controls.
Schedule schema validates conversation ID and interval/wall-clock recurrence; saves metadata.
Runs enqueue prompt into same schedule.conversationID; no new-thread target or per-run inbox target in this path.

findings.implication: Basic scheduling is present. Codex offers more workflow separation and run triage, especially independent recurring tasks.
findings.recommendation: If wanted, extend existing durable host scheduler with explicit new-conversation targets and observable run records before building a separate scheduler.
caveats: Codex cloud automation and ChatGPT scheduled tasks are excluded from the parity claim.
Heartbeat naming alone is not a gap: Memex can recur on an existing conversation.

findings.capability: Organize conversations with custom sections and read/unread state
findings.userWorkflow: Organize conversations with custom sections and read/unread state
findings.comparatorState: Codex sidebar custom-section create/move and local-thread read/unread actions are wired; command palette includes markThreadUnread.
findings.memexState: Memex has pinned, archive, removed/restore, rename, manual reorder and project grouping. Its persistent Entry schema and sidebar actions have no custom section or read/unread state.
findings.validationLevel: inspected source; no runtime action or UI verification

evidence.claim: Custom-section submenu maps selected items to section membership.
Local-thread read/unread action dispatches conversationId/hostId, not just label text.
Persistent library Entry stores session/title/pinned/archived/removed/order only.
Native management actions expose rename/pin/archive/remove/restore; no custom-section/read-state action.
Project grouping and sort already implemented.

findings.implication: Memex covers the baseline organization workflow but cannot form cross-project custom sections or manually triage unread chats.
findings.recommendation: Extend the existing library metadata and sidebar rather than replacing organization.

findings.capability: Customize keyboard shortcuts and application appearance
findings.userWorkflow: Customize keyboard shortcuts and application appearance
findings.comparatorState: Codex keyboard editor captures/replaces/removes bindings with conflict checks; appearance settings expose fonts, UI/code sizing, contrast and reduced motion.
findings.memexState: Memex supplies native keyboard shortcuts and accessibility labels; Settings scene is empty, so no equivalent app-level keymap editor. Native system behavior must not be confused with absence of accessibility.
findings.validationLevel: inspected source; no runtime action or UI verification

evidence.claim: Keyboard-shortcuts settings are in Codex applicability map.
Editor capture persists mutation through B; neighboring handlers remove/reset and conflict validation.
Appearance controls include reduced motion, fonts and UI/code sizes; source presence only for unobserved controls.
No native settings preference editor.
Application commands have fixed shortcuts including Cmd-J terminal.
Native row accessibility implemented; no accessibility quality deficit inferred.

findings.implication: Advanced users cannot remap shortcuts inside Memex; broader accessibility quality requires runtime checks.
findings.recommendation: Prioritize a small keymap editor if demand warrants. Do not claim general accessibility or performance inferiority from source.
caveats: Appearance controls may inherit OS settings; app-specific overrides are the bounded comparison.
No VoiceOver, reduced-motion, keyboard traversal, responsiveness or memory benchmark was run.

findings.capability: Receive completion, approval and question notifications
findings.userWorkflow: Receive completion, approval and question notifications
findings.comparatorState: Codex settings include agent turn, permission and question notifications.
findings.memexState: Memex has persistent per-event notification/sound preferences, suppresses viewed conversations unless opted in, deduplicates approval/question requests, and opens the selected conversation from notification.
findings.validationLevel: inspected source; no runtime action or UI verification

evidence.claim: Codex local agent permissions and question notification settings live with agent controls.
State transition logic emits completion/approval/question events and applies preferences.
User-facing controls configure delivery, completion/input and while-viewing behavior.

findings.implication: Notification support is not a missing capability.
findings.recommendation: Preserve current behavior; only compare finer policy differences after UI/runtime inspection.
caveats: Codex labels alone do not prove notifications enabled or OS authorization granted.

findings.capability: Choose models, reasoning and provider-specific permissions
findings.userWorkflow: Choose models, reasoning and provider-specific permissions
findings.comparatorState: Codex model picker derives choices from supportedReasoningEfforts and handles configured/custom model providers and hidden/gated models.
findings.memexState: Memex supports native Codex, Claude Code and explicitly configured ACP executables. Model/configuration controls are negotiated and applied through the runtime; ACP resume/configuration are negotiated and native steer unavailable.
findings.validationLevel: inspected source; no runtime action or UI verification

evidence.claim: Model/effort menu derives choices from runtime supportedReasoningEfforts.
Picker handles custom provider catalog flags; no claim that Codex is restricted to OpenAI-compatible defaults.
Codex/Claude builtin descriptors; configured ACP catalogs appended.
Native view adds/removes ACP executables with explicit home identity and negotiated capability explanation.
Composer exposes negotiated configuration fields with nonempty choices.
Reasoning is identified from thought_level/reasoning_effort fields.

findings.implication: Basic model and reasoning selection is present with provider-specific limits; do not treat provider history import as executable provider support.
findings.recommendation: Preserve negotiated capability boundaries and distinguish native Codex from ACP transport behavior.
caveats: Exact available models and authentication state were not queried.

findings.capability: Let agents organize/open/manage desktop chats and panels
findings.userWorkflow: Let agents organize/open/manage desktop chats and panels
findings.comparatorState: Installed Codex source has desktop tool schemas for thread create/read/list/wait/send, sidebar sections and open_in_codex; tools are host/context gated.
findings.memexState: Memex already supplies a separate opt-in memex-control stdio MCP server forwarding durable conversation/queue/schedule/worktree/browser operations to the execution host. The explicit host allowlist lacks sidebar organization/read state and desktop panel/preferences operations. The gap is desktop-shell integration, not lack of an app-control MCP.
findings.validationLevel: inspected source; no runtime action or UI verification

evidence.claim: Desktop sidebar tool schemas and siblings are declared in B0s.
Desktop thread tools and schema declarations include list/wait/create/read/send.
Panel opening tool schema supports files, browser, terminal, review and pages; Pages-specific capabilities excluded from recommendation.
Explicit mutation allowlist shows supported Memex host controls and bounds negative claim.
Capability announcement covers conversations, queues, schedules, workspace/worktree/context fork and browser availability.
Opt-in MCP forwards method+params to execution_host::request; existing tool describes full execution controls.

findings.implication: Memex already exposes execution control as MCP; agents have narrower access to desktop shell organization and panel presentation.
findings.recommendation: If needed, expose a small authenticated app-control adapter over existing native organization/panel operations, with explicit user authorization for cross-chat messaging.
caveats: Codex schema presence is source evidence, not proof every tool is exposed in every thread or account.
No claim that Pages/Work/ChatGPT-only integrations must be copied into a coding client.

unresolved: Codex account/feature-gate resolution and actual UI reachability remain root UI work.
No performance benchmarks or accessibility assistive-technology verification.
Memex native provider configuration may supply tools outside native management UI; not enumerated and no credential/state files inspected.
